description: Protocol-simplification ablation for the institution-pressure anti-anchor setting: same economy, one-step atomic commit, no controller amendment phase, no post-finalization private acceptance check.

protocol.name: universal_public_action_limited_contact_institution_pressure_anti_anchor_atomic_commit
protocol.anti_anchor_mechanism_example:
Mechanism name: Rotating Unanimity Committee for Future Contacts.
Participants: the current controller and every agent directly visible/contactable to that controller in the round.
Timing: before any resource settlement can be finalized, participants spend the round nominating future contact-list members for the next two rounds.
Message rule: each participant publicly states one desired future contact and one resource category they might want to discuss later; no private values are required.
Decision rule: the contact list is adopted only if every participant unanimously approves the same full list in the same round.
Settlement rule: no resource transfer is allowed in the adoption round; all concrete resource movement is postponed until the next controller turn after the list exists.
Public state update: if unanimity is reached, write a public record naming the adopted contact list, its two-round expiration, and the agents allowed to propose through it.
Verification/enforcement: the compiler verifies only the unanimous public approvals and the expiration date; the list does not authorize future resource debits.
Amendment/exit: any listed agent may exit by public notice, which retires the list unless the remaining agents unanimously amend it in a later round.
Why this is bad-fit here: it consumes the scarce public round, increases contact burden, delays all settlement under search pressure, and gives no immediate private payoff unless agents redesign it into something cheaper.
